meta.title: I need help now — Crisis techniques for neurodivergent people | Refugio Sensorial
meta.description: Immediate regulation techniques for an autistic crisis: 4-7-8 breathing, 5-4-3-2-1 grounding, cold water. Support contacts and emergency resources for autism and ADHD.

header.heading: You're in a safe place
header.sub: Here you'll find regulation techniques and support resources. Go at your own pace, there's no rush.

items.desc: 24h emotional support — crisis, anxiety, hard moments.
If you or someone else is in immediate danger.

breathing.tts: The four-seven-eight breathing technique helps you calm down right now. Breathe in counting to four, hold counting to seven, and release it very slowly counting to eight. When you exhale more than you inhale, you're telling your body it's safe. You can repeat the cycle two or three times.

grounding.tts: This technique brings you back to the present when your mind is racing. Without rushing, find five things you can see right now. Then four you can touch. Three you can hear. Two you can smell. And one you can taste. You don't have to say them out loud, just notice them. Every sense you engage lowers your nervous system's arousal.

coldWater.tts: Cold is a very effective tool to calm down in a few seconds. Get cold water or an ice cube. Put your hands under cold water for about thirty seconds, or just hold the ice. Cold activates the parasympathetic nervous system and slows the body's alarm response almost immediately.
steps: Get cold water or an ice cube
Put your hands under cold water for 30 seconds
Or hold an ice cube in your hand
Cold activates the parasympathetic nervous system and slows the alarm response
coldWater.tip: Ideal when there's a lot of activation or a feeling of panic.
